name: Close the books each month
summary: At the end of every month the controllership team turns the month's activity into a trial balance and results that management can rely on. Accountants settle maintenance and project costs, accrue costs not yet invoiced, book pool revenue from the company's own meter data before the system operator's statements arrive, value hedges at month-end prices with the risk group, reconcile every balance sheet account and explain variances. The work is slow because many pieces wait on outside statements, estimates must later be trued up, and each review can send entries back for correction before the controller locks the period.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant power generator listed on the TSX and NYSE, with an ERP general ledger, a trading and risk system for hedges and a controllership group of about 40 including AP.
baseline.notes: Close run in spreadsheets and the ERP with a close checklist; no dedicated close-management software assumed.

end_state: The period is locked and the trial balance and monthly results are released to reporting, planning and tax.

volume.seasonality: Quarter-end months add the tax provision and more review ahead of quarterly reporting; year end adds the external audit.

evidence.note: One close per month by definition.

Organisation file lists 18 accountants in controllership. About 5 FTE of their month goes to close entries, accruals and reconciliations; the rest is AP oversight, fixed assets, joint venture billing, audit support and quarterly reporting. Estimate.

A listed company with 18 accountants has two or three accounting managers between the accountants and the controller who review reconciliations and run consolidation; the organisation file has all accountants reporting straight to the controller. Cost set at the asset manager rate in the organisation file.
Reviews results and locks the period each month. Estimate.
Pool revenue accrual, final-statement true-ups and trade settlement accruals at month end. Estimate.
Month-end mark-to-market valuation and price verification. Estimate.
Interest, foreign exchange and bank reconciliation entries. Estimate.
Monthly results package and variance commentary. Estimate.

systems.name: ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)
Energy trading and risk management system
AESO Energy Trading System (offers, declarations and dispatch)

steps.name: Confirm sub-ledger cut-offs
steps.description: On the first working day the close lead accountant checks the close calendar, confirms with AP, payroll, settlement and treasury that their month's postings are complete, and opens the next period for operational postings while keeping the closing period open for finance only.

error.defect_description: A sub-ledger posts into the closed month after cut-off.

evidence.note: Month end often falls on a weekend or holiday, delaying the first working day. Estimate.

steps.name: Settle work orders to cost centres and projects
steps.description: The ERP's overnight settlement run moves labour, materials and contractor costs collected on maintenance work orders and capital or outage projects to their cost centres and asset-under-construction accounts.

error.defect_description: Work orders without a valid settlement rule leave costs unsettled.

evidence.note: Standard plant maintenance and project settlement in an ERP. Estimate.

steps.name: Review work order settlement and capital allocations
steps.description: An accountant works through the settlement error log, adds missing settlement rules, and checks that outage and conversion project costs are split correctly between maintenance expense and capital under the capitalisation policy.

error.defect_description: Maintenance cost capitalised or capital cost expensed.

control.basis: IFRS capitalisation policy reviewed under internal control over financial reporting

steps.name: Accrue goods and services received but not invoiced
steps.description: An accountant runs the received-not-invoiced report, asks plant and outage managers for contractor work done but not yet billed, and books accruals with reversal for the next month.

error.defect_description: Contractor work in progress under- or over-accrued.

steps.name: Accrue pool revenue from metered generation
steps.description: The settlement analyst totals each asset's metered or dispatched output for the month from the historian and the AESO trading system, prices it at the hourly pool price, adds ancillary service revenue and books the revenue accrual before the AESO's statements arrive.

error.defect_description: Meter data gaps or wrong asset mapping misstate revenue.

evidence.note: The AESO preliminary statement comes after the close starts, so generators accrue from their own data and true up later (organisation file process description). Estimate.

steps.name: Book true-up from the AESO final statement
steps.description: The settlement analyst compares the AESO final statement for the earlier month, received during the closing month, with the accrual booked at that close and posts the difference, explaining any large gap.

error.defect_description: True-up booked twice or to the wrong month.

evidence.note: AESO statement timing (preliminary around the fifth and final around the fifteenth business day) is from general knowledge; estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile and accrue trade settlements
steps.description: The settlement analyst matches physical and financial power and gas trades in the trading system with counterparty invoices and exchange clearing statements as they arrive, and accrues the trades whose statements are not yet in.

error.defect_description: A trade accrued at the wrong price or missed.

evidence.note: Counterparty and exchange statements arrive over the first working days. Estimate.

steps.name: Value derivatives at month-end forward prices
steps.description: The risk analyst loads month-end forward curves, checks broker quotes against them, runs the mark-to-market valuation of open power, gas and emissions hedges in the trading system and sends the valuation report with changes explained to accounting.

error.defect_description: Stale curve point or wrong hedge designation.

control.basis: Independent price verification of derivative valuations by the middle office

evidence.note: Independent risk group using limits is stated for the modelled company in the organisation file; valuation effort is an estimate.

steps.name: Post unrealised gains and hedge entries
steps.description: An accountant reviews the mark-to-market report, posts unrealised gains and losses and hedge accounting entries by portfolio, and reconciles the derivative asset and liability balances to the report.

error.defect_description: Entry posted to the wrong hedge relationship.

steps.name: Accrue fuel, carbon and customer revenue
steps.description: An accountant books gas cost from nominations and supplier estimates, the carbon compliance cost on the month's emissions at the carbon price in force, and customer and cogeneration revenue from the billing system.

error.defect_description: Emissions volume or carbon price wrong.

steps.name: Accrue payroll, incentives and partner costs
steps.description: An accountant accrues wages for days worked since the last pay day, vacation and incentive plans, and the company's share of partner-operated plant costs from the operator's estimate until its billing arrives.

error.defect_description: Partner cost estimate off when the operator billing differs.

steps.name: Run depreciation and reclamation accretion
steps.description: An accountant runs depreciation in the fixed asset module, transfers completed projects into service, and books accretion on decommissioning and mine reclamation provisions.

error.defect_description: Asset placed in service in the wrong month.

steps.name: Record treasury entries and bank reconciliations
steps.description: The treasury analyst accrues interest on debt, revalues US dollar balances at the month-end rate, and reconciles each bank account to the bank statement downloaded from the bank portal.

error.defect_description: Unrecorded bank item left as a reconciling difference.

steps.name: Reconcile balance sheet accounts
steps.description: Accountants reconcile each balance sheet account in their area to its sub-ledger, schedule or third-party statement in standard reconciliation templates, explain and clear reconciling items, and attach support.

error.defect_description: Unexplained item carried forward instead of cleared.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: periodic account reconciliation

evidence.note: About 300 balance sheet accounts are split among six to eight accountants who work in parallel; touch shown is the longest single accountant's share (critical path), about a third of the combined effort.

steps.name: Review and sign off reconciliations
steps.description: The accounting manager reviews the reconciliations for key and high-risk accounts, checks that reconciling items are explained and aged, and signs them off or returns them with questions.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Review and sign-off of reconciliations supporting CEO and CFO certification of internal control

steps.name: Run preliminary trial balance and flux analysis
steps.description: An accountant runs the preliminary trial balance and compares each line with the prior month, the same month last year and the forecast, flagging variances above set thresholds for explanation.

error.defect_description: A large variance explained away without checking.

steps.name: Investigate variances and post corrections
steps.description: The responsible accountant traces each unexplained variance to its entries, finds misposted or missing items, and books correcting journals with support after review by a second accountant.

error.defect_description: Correction introduces another error.

control.basis: Manual journals prepared and approved by different people

steps.name: Consolidate entities and eliminate intercompany balances
steps.description: The accounting manager runs consolidation of the operating partnerships and subsidiaries, eliminates intercompany sales, loans and management fees, and checks that intercompany balances agree on both sides.

error.defect_description: Intercompany mismatch forced through elimination.

steps.name: Prepare quarter-end tax provision
steps.description: In quarter-end months the tax specialist computes current and deferred income tax for each entity from the consolidated results, updates temporary differences for capital and decommissioning items and books the provision.

error.defect_description: Deferred tax on a new temporary difference missed.

steps.name: Prepare results package and commentary
steps.description: The planning analyst builds the monthly results package from the consolidated trial balance: gross margin by segment, operating costs and capital spending against budget and forecast, with written explanations gathered from business unit leads.

error.defect_description: Commentary attributes a variance to the wrong cause.

steps.name: Controller reviews results
steps.description: The corporate controller reviews the trial balance, the flux analysis and the results package, questions unusual movements and judgement areas such as accruals and provisions, and either accepts the results or asks for adjustments.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Management review control over monthly results

steps.name: Lock period and release trial balance
steps.description: The controller approves the final adjustments, locks the period in the ERP so that no further postings can be made without controller approval, and releases the trial balance to reporting, planning and tax.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Period lock and controller approval of post-close entries

steps.name: Publish trial balance and management reports
steps.description: The reporting system refreshes from the locked ledger and publishes the trial balance, segment reports and dashboards to executives, planning, tax and the quarterly reporting team.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

exceptions.name: Reconciliations returned
exceptions.description: The accounting manager returns reconciliations with unexplained items for rework.

exceptions.name: Corrections after flux review
exceptions.description: The preliminary trial balance shows variances caused by misposted or missing entries, which are corrected before the trial balance is rerun.

exceptions.name: Controller adjustments
exceptions.description: The controller questions an accrual or provision and asks for an adjustment, sending the close back through the flux review.

exceptions.name: Quarter-end tax provision
exceptions.description: In March, June, September and December the tax provision is added before results are reviewed.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from running the trial balance to completed consolidated monthly statements
benchmarks.population: APQC General Accounting Open Standards Benchmarking, 2,300 organisations (published 2018)

evidence.note: Median 6.4 days; the 10 shown as p90 is APQC's bottom-quartile threshold (10 days or more), not a 90th percentile. APQC's clock starts when the trial balance is first run, after the first day or two of month-end processing that this workflow includes.

pain_points.description: Pool revenue, trade settlements and partner costs are booked on estimates because outside statements arrive after the close, and each month's close also has to absorb true-ups for earlier months.

evidence.note: Organisation file process description notes that final AESO statements arrive later; rest is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Work order settlement errors and capital versus expense splits on outage and conversion projects take manual review every month.
Reconciliations and flux reviews send entries back for rework, and the controller's review often triggers another round.

sources.title: Metric of the Month: Cycle Time for Monthly Close
sources.publisher: CFO.com (APQC General Accounting Open Standards Benchmarking)
sources.supports: Calendar days from running the trial balance to completing the consolidated monthly financial statements, 2,300 organisations: median 6.4 days, top quartile 4.8 days or less, bottom quartile 10 days or more; includes waiting time.

assumptions: Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40). The accounting manager role is added with not_in_org_file.
The close starts at midnight on the last day of the month and ends when the controller releases the trial balance; the APQC benchmark starts later, at the first trial balance run.
Steps that run at the same time in practice (pool revenue, AP accruals, treasury entries, derivative valuation) are listed in sequence with near-zero waits and named in concurrent_with.

Validator check: simulated median cycle time is about 11.5 calendar days (p90 15.4), roughly the seventh or eighth working day. The first preliminary trial balance (step s16) comes after a median of about 7.4 days, so the stretch comparable with the APQC measure (trial balance to final results) is about 4 days, between APQC's top quartile (4.8) and median (6.4). Listing parallel steps in sequence adds about a day to the simulated total.

Staffing check (warning left on purpose): roles state 9.4 FTE but hands-on time implies about 0.9 FTE. Step touch times follow the critical path so that the simulated cycle stays realistic: the reconciliation step shows one accountant's share of about 300 accounts, and much close work (journal preparation during the month, supporting schedules, audit requests, reviewers' questions) is not itemised. Stated FTE reflect how much of the 18 accountants' and the analysts' time the close takes in a typical month.
